findings.claim: The new requirement to name an actual merge commit is ambiguous for squash and fast-forward landings, which have no Git merge commit. The reference itself anticipates a squashed branch whose reviewed head was deleted. A reader following the new wording may leave an otherwise landed change waiting for closure or omit its resolvable t1.
proof_refs: Changed lines 30-31 require the parent to name the actual merge commit; line 33 explicitly discusses a squashed branch.
At the base, lines 27-28 required the explicitly recorded commit that landed delivery without restricting it to a merge commit.
